<a id="development"></a>

# Development

The repository has two check scripts: `scripts/check.ps1` on Windows and `scripts/check.sh` on Unix. They run the formatter check, vet, the build and the tests.

Run the test suite and the race detector through the scripts. The suite covers the model, the store, the structure path, rendering, the editorial features, the grammar client, the repository layout, search and the index, apply, migrations, badges, ASCII UI layouts and the terminal view models.

CI runs three jobs on pushes to `main` that change the build-version file, and on manual dispatch: a verify job for the formatter, vet, build and tests, a race job and a Windows job.

A `v*` tag runs the separate release workflow: it verifies the tree, builds the six platform archives, writes `SHA256SUMS` and publishes the GitHub Release. Use `scripts/release.ps1` (Windows) or `scripts/release.sh` (Unix) to validate and push the tag; CI never creates it. The build-version file only triggers the verify CI; it is still changed at each scope close.

Layering: command packages carry the CLI surface, and pure packages never import it. The core services are plain Go and can be used in process, which is what the terminal UI does.

All mutations go through one structure path: lock, rollback package, validation, atomic write. A command must not write the manifest or a body directly.

Rendering is pure and deterministic. Tests assert the rendered lines and the golden output, not terminal escape sequences, and the race detector must stay clean.

A contribution opens a book, makes its changes through the commands, runs `sync --check` and `verify`, and commits the rendered output together with the source changes it belongs to.
